source_name: НБРМ — Платежна статистика (payment statistics)
why_relevant: Official payment statistics: cards issued, ATM and POS terminal counts, transaction volumes/values by instrument and channel. The benchmark dataset against which any operator or vendor claim about the MK payments market is checked.

source_name: НБРМ — Платежни институции, институции за електронски пари и оператори на платни системи (register)
why_relevant: The licensing register: authoritative, enumerable list of every licensed payment institution, e-money institution and payment-system operator in MK. The canonical actor-map seed for this cell — new entrants appear here before they appear anywhere else.

source_name: НБРМ — Регулатива за платните системи и платежните услуги + подзаконски акти (ЗПУПС)
why_relevant: The Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (ЗПУПС, PSD2-aligned) and its secondary acts define who may operate a scheme/switch, licensing thresholds, and open-banking obligations — the rule layer that reshapes the operator landscape.

source_name: НБРМ — CaSys system oversight page (International Card System AD)
why_relevant: Regulator's own description of CaSys as a designated payment system (multilateral deferred net settlement for domestic-brand cards; operates banks' ATM and POS networks with authorisation/switching). Independent confirmation of the switch's role and settlement linkage into MIPS.

source_name: National instant-payment initiative (TIPS clone / Western Balkans) — NBRM announcements as carried by MK media
why_relevant: The single biggest structural change in MK payments infrastructure: connection to a TIPS clone for 24/7 instant payments, alongside Albania and Kosovo, with proxy-lookup (pay-by-mobile-number) planned. Media carry NBRM statements with dates and milestones that are not always on the bank's own news page.

source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (ecommerce.mk)
why_relevant: The e-commerce association republishes processor and acquirer press releases verbatim (e.g. CaSys new payment products, first 'Pay by link' service in MK, 15 years of the first electronic transaction) and runs an annual conference whose sponsor list is a live map of MK payment vendors.

source_name: Diners Club Macedonia — Дајнерс Клуб Интернационал МАК (diners.mk)
why_relevant: Franchise scheme operator for the Diners Club brand in MK (first credit/payment card in the country, 1996). A non-bank card issuer/acceptor whose franchise ownership changed hands — a distinct scheme actor outside the Visa/Mastercard duopoly.

source_name: Payten / Asseco South Eastern Europe (ASEE) — regional payments vendor newsroom
why_relevant: Major regional supplier of ATM/POS software and services, processing and acquiring, and operator of the MoneyGet independent ATM network across SEE. Vendor news and ASEE investor reporting reveal contract wins and terminal-estate movements that operators themselves do not announce.

source_name: Mastercard / Visa market announcements for North Macedonia (via MK tech & business media)
why_relevant: International scheme go-lives in MK (Google Pay/Google Wallet via Mastercard; Apple Pay launch) are announced through schemes and issuing banks and reported by MK tech media. These mark acceptance-infrastructure and tokenisation milestones for the whole market.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — member directory (CaSys and payment-sector members)
why_relevant: Business-chamber member profiles give current self-descriptions, leadership names and contact points for payment operators, and the wider directory enumerates adjacent fintech/vendor actors for snowballing.

source_name: Faktor.mk — payments-industry business reporting
why_relevant: Business daily that covers ownership changes and transaction values in the MK payments industry (e.g. reporting on a EUR 12m stake purchase in the payments industry, e-money developments, scheme launches) — the kind of deal detail neither operator nor regulator publishes.

source_name: Iute Group corporate news (IutePay Macedonia)
why_relevant: Listed Baltic group whose Skopje subsidiary IutePay DOOEL obtained an EMI licence in MK; because the parent is bond-listed it issues formal, dated releases on MK wallet/QR/cardless-ATM rollout — rare disclosure-grade PR for a MK payments actor.

source_name: Nayax newsroom — Balkan/North Macedonia market entries
why_relevant: Foreign PSP/unattended-payments vendor that announced full cashless acceptance in MK; template case of a cross-border acquirer entering the market, announced only via corporate PR.

source_name: Flex Pay (Флекс пеј) — licensed MK e-money institution
why_relevant: One of the newest domestic EMI licensees; a target actor whose product launches will define local wallet competition. Own corporate domain not confirmed in this pass — currently trackable only through media carrying its releases.

source_name: mkPay (МКПЕЈ) — bill-payment platform / prospective e-money issuer
why_relevant: Domestic bill-payment platform reported to be preparing e-money issuance and 'the first Macedonian e-wallet' with QR payments; a bellwether for domestic (non-bank) wallet competition.

source_name: MINT Fintech Group — Macedonian super-app (payments, FX, loyalty)
source_subtype: company announcement carried by business media
why_relevant: Local group launching an integrated app bundling payments, insurance, loyalty, travel and FX — exactly the kind of product-launch signal this cell exists to catch. Official domain unconfirmed; currently reachable through mk business media.

source_name: Paysera Macedonia — first licensed MK e-money institution
why_relevant: Reported as the first EMI licensed by NBRM; a pan-European wallet operator localising in MK. Its MK-country site/blog is the natural place for local product and partnership announcements. URL is the conventional country domain and was NOT confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Halkbank AD Skopje — Western Union agency & HalkPay wallet
why_relevant: Authorised Western Union agent for MK and operator of the HalkPay wallet; sits at the intersection of remittances and QR/NFC wallet competition, and announces both via its own site.

source_name: Stopanska Banka AD Skopje — payment services / Western Union pages
why_relevant: Major acquirer and remittance payout channel; publishes service terms and offer PDFs that reveal remittance corridor pricing and product changes.

source_name: UFS (Универзал Финанс Сервис) — money-transfer locations MK
why_relevant: Non-bank money-transfer operator/agent network in MK — the kind of remittance actor that never files IR documents and is visible only via its own site.

source_name: Startup Macedonia — startup ecosystem platform
why_relevant: Data-driven registry of MK startups; the practical way to spot pre-licence payment/fintech startups and funding rounds before they reach trade press.

source_name: FintechMK community (Fintech.mk) — Facebook page
why_relevant: The self-described first MK fintech community; social channels are where small MK payment startups actually announce launches. Platform is bot-hostile, so treat as manual/low-frequency.

source_name: TheRecursive.com — SEE startup & fintech funding coverage
why_relevant: Regional outlet that profiles Macedonian fintech startups and their funding/partnership news in English — the main English-language route to MK fintech company news.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — North Macedonia payments/fintech reporting
why_relevant: Emerging-markets business wire that covers foreign PSP market entries into MK (e.g. Nayax) with more context than a corporate release; good for cross-checking claims.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — MK e-payment landscape guide
why_relevant: Structured explainer of the MK e-payment stack: which processor runs the gateway and which banks provide acquiring. Efficient way to bootstrap the acquirer/PSP actor map and its aliases.

source_name: Google Play / App Store listings for MK payment apps (release notes)
why_relevant: For MK wallet issuers (MkPay, HalkPay, NLB Pay, MyIute, mona) the app-store changelog is often the only dated, machine-readable record of feature launches — QR, NFC, SoftPOS, BNPL — since these firms rarely issue formal PR.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom - Europe (press releases & news briefs)
why_relevant: Scheme-level country announcements naming MK institutions. Confirmed to carry MK items, e.g. the Republic of North Macedonia National Digital Identity Service launch (Nov 2021) which names NLB Banka Skopje as first user and Evrotrust as operator - a bank-technology fact no MK bank published itself.
